heredoc-stdin-script._note: When a heredoc's reader runs its body: only when the program takes its SCRIPT from stdin (stdinIsScript and its STDIN_FLAGS table, the same in both guards). A script file named, or a script handed as -c / -e / -p / -m, makes the body that program's input data (`bash ./run.sh <<EOF`, `node -e '...' <<EOF`); each option word is read the way that interpreter's own parser reads it (one STDIN_FLAGS row each for the shells, node, python, ruby, perl and php), so an option's own value, bundled or the next word, is no script file (`bash -euo pipefail`, `bash --rcfile x`, `node -r ./x.js`, `node --max-old-space-size 4096`, `python3 -Q new`, `perl -Mstrict -we`); an option the table does not know takes the next word as its value, and a script option with no script word leaves the body the script; a runtime's `-` (and php's `--`) is stdin itself and the words after it are the script's argv (`python3 - <file> <<EOF`), while a shell's `-` or `--` only ends its options; a program with no row (deno, bun, pwsh) always runs its body. The read guard judges a shell body as commands since 2.1.6 round 4; the secret guard judged every runtime or shell body as code.
